title: Ser: soy, eres, es… y vosotros
summary: The verb ser for who and where from — with the full paradigm including vosotros

blocks.title: ser — the 'this is who/what I am' verb
blocks.body: **ser** tells people who you are and where you're from — identity and origin. It's irregular, so learn the whole set now. Note the two you-plural forms: **vosotros** (informal, the Spain default for a group of friends) and *ustedes* (formal). In Spain you'll use **vosotros** constantly.

blocks.title: ¿De dónde eres?
blocks.body: To ask where someone's from: **¿de dónde eres?** To answer: *soy de…* + a place, or *soy* + a nationality. Nationalities agree with gender: *soy irlandés / soy irlandesa*, *soy canadiense* (same for both). Names use *me llamo…* (literally 'I call myself').
blocks.callout: *Soy de Londres* (I'm from London) or *soy inglés/inglesa* (I'm English) — both work.

blocks.prompt: You're talking to a group of friends and want to say 'you all are'. Which form?
blocks.explain: *sois* — the **vosotros** form, the informal you-plural you'll use nonstop in Spain. *son* is for ellos/ustedes; *somos* is 'we'.
*Soy de Madrid.* Origin = ser, first person = soy.
